To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have presented a novel parameterization of the three-nucleon wave function, and that this parameterization is suitable for calculations of two-body currents.
a novel parameterization of the complete wave function of the trinuclear system has been presented and applied in an analysis of π3He scattering.
a new parameterization for the trinucleons wave function was developed, that it is separable, and that the π3He-scattering length was calculated using the new parameterization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the pion-triton scattering amplitude in chiral-potential theory.
the development of an effective field theory for the trinucleons and the application of this theory to the π3He system.
the study of the π3He and π4He systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the πN scattering length aπN is known with a precision of ±0.001.
the πN scattering data are not yet sufficient to fix all parameters of the chiral expansion and that a more detailed analysis of π3He data is needed.
the π-triton scattering length can be calculated to a precision of a few percent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the π-triton bound system can be used to obtain information on πN scattering lengths.
a parameterization of the three-nucleon wave function that includes the full wave function is possible and that it can be applied to calculations in chiral perturbation theory.
a new parameterization for the trinucleons has been presented and the π3He-scattering length has been calculated with the result a1 = 0.14 fm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to describe pionic atoms with the same accuracy as free pion scattering, without the necessity to use a full trinucleon Faddeev calculation.
the trinucleonic system provides a rich playground for the investigation of the interplay between few-nucleon physics and chiral dynamics.
a new parameterization has been developed that allows for a more efficient calculation of two-body currents in trinucleons.
